recipe.title: Light Relay
recipe.summary: Rotate mirrors. Route one beam through three optical puzzles.

steps.title: Build Light Relay
steps.text:
Create a complete standalone light-relay.html with inline CSS and JavaScript: a three-chamber light-routing puzzle. No dependencies, network, storage, external assets, eval, forms, or audio. Include meta CSP exactly: default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; connect-src 'none'. Work inside iframe sandbox='allow-scripts' with an opaque origin. After synchronous initialization, call window.parent.postMessage({type:'pls-demo-ready'}, '*').

Visual direction: a near-black instrument panel (#080808), inset 7-by-7 square circuit board, thin gray cell borders, white labels, system monospace controls, a large condensed sans-serif LIGHT RELAY heading, warm amber active beam and cool cyan receiver. Keep color inside the game. This is geometric circuit visualization, not an illustration. Desktop: board left, compact mission/control panel right. Below 700px stack board before panel. Use readable rem text (body 16px, controls 14px), minimum 44px action targets, strong visible focus, no motion required, and fit at 320px without horizontal scrolling or clipped text. Display the primary puzzle in the first viewport with brief instructions: Rotate mirrors. Connect the light to the receiver.

Rules: 7 rows and 7 columns, coordinates below are zero-based [row,column]. Source occupies its listed cell and sends light east. Receiver occupies its listed cell. Walls absorb light. Empty cells transmit straight. Mirrors stay in their fixed cells and toggle between / and backslash on activation. Use direction indices E=0,S=1,W=2,N=3. Slash maps [3,2,1,0]; backslash maps [1,0,3,2]. Trace one cell at a time from source to outside board, wall, receiver, or repeated (row,column,direction). Only reaching receiver solves. Draw connected segments through cell centers with SVG over the board; make its layer pointer-events:none and aria-hidden. Actual mirror buttons below/above it must remain clickable. Keep lit-cell state and a plain text path description (one-based cell coordinates) available in a details disclosure, so light color is not the sole feedback. Use an aria-live status for changes, not frame updates. No timer.

Chambers, with mirror triples [row,column,orientation] (use '/' or backslash):
1. FIRST CONTACT: source [4,0], receiver [1,6], mirrors initially [4,2,backslash],[1,2,backslash]; solution both '/'; walls [0,4],[2,4],[3,4],[5,4]. Optimal solution from initial board: 2 rotations.
2. DOGLEG: source [5,0], receiver [1,6], mirrors initially [5,2,backslash],[2,2,backslash],[2,4,'/'],[1,4,backslash]; solution in that same order ['/','/','/','/']; walls [3,3],[4,4],[0,1],[6,5]. Optimal: 3 rotations.
3. LONG WAY HOME: source [5,0], receiver [1,6], mirrors initially [5,1,backslash],[3,1,backslash],[3,3,'/'],[5,3,'/'],[5,5,backslash],[1,5,backslash]; solution ['/','/','backslash','backslash','/','/']; walls [2,2],[4,4],[0,3],[6,3]. Optimal: 6 rotations.

Render source as a right arrow and receiver as a ring, with visible S and R identifiers in their cells and accessible text. Render walls as crosshatch or #. Each mirror is a real type=button with data-cell='row,column', one-based accessible label naming row, column and slash/backslash orientation, and aria-pressed=true for slash. Clicking/Enter/Space toggles it, increments rotations once, saves undo history, retraces light, and retains focus. Board arrow keys move focus among mirror buttons in row-major order: Right/Down next, Left/Up previous, wrapping. Include a persistent legend.

Show chamber name, chamber number, rotations, optimal rotations, and session best (dash until solved). Add an ordered chamber selector; first unlocked initially, later chambers unlock only when the previous is solved. Undo reverts one rotation and decrements count, disables when empty; retain unlocks and bests on undo. Reset chamber restores its initial orientations/count/history and keeps session best/unlocks. Hint outlines the first mirror differing from its solution and announces its one-based coordinates, without rotating or incrementing count; clear old hint on rotation/undo/reset/chamber change. Hint usage must be visibly counted per attempt and recorded beside session best: best is lowest rotations, then fewest hints on ties. Undo does not erase hint usage. Reset sets attempt hints to zero. Solving unlocks the next chamber and enables Next chamber; final completion reads All three chambers connected. Re-entering any unlocked chamber starts its initial board. On solution keep mirrors and Undo available; further moves can unsolve without revoking earned unlocks. Provide Reset all that restores chamber 1, all initial states, no bests, no hints, and only first unlocked. Disable Next chamber when current board is not solved or final. Initial board must not appear solved. User text input is unnecessary.

steps.title: Verify and repair
steps.text: Test inside an allow-scripts-only iframe with the exact CSP. Confirm all three chambers start unsolved and solve using the listed mirror orientations. Check rotation counts 2,3,6 from initial states, undo, reset, session best/hint tie handling, locked chamber buttons, next-chamber gating, final completion, hint coordinates without movement, Enter/Space and arrow focus, and full reset. Check at 320,375,768,1024,1440,1600px and 200% root text at 320px. Confirm no horizontal overflow, external requests, script errors, or storage access. Repairs identified during this build: explicitly set seven equal CSS grid rows so beam centers match cells; render the SVG above opaque mirror backgrounds while retaining pointer-events:none; allow narrow chamber buttons and board-header labels to shrink/wrap at 200% root text. Keep fixed board symbols small enough to fit each cell at enlarged root text, while body and controls still scale. Preserve every puzzle rule and control. Repair any other issues found and return the corrected standalone file. Report actual checks and any untested behavior; do not claim one-shot, pixel-identical, or cross-browser reproduction.

recipe.setup: Open an empty directory in Codex. Paste Step 1, then Step 2 in the same task. Open light-relay.html in a modern browser or serve the directory with any static server. No packages, accounts, keys, images or paid services are required. All progress exists only until reload. The gallery supplies its own separate host chrome.
recipe.customize: Change chamber coordinates and walls, validating each route with the trace algorithm. Adjust board/beam colors while preserving contrast and non-color status. More chambers require matching initial mirrors, solutions, and optimal rotation counts. Geometry is fixed at 7x7 unless layout and bounds change together.
recipe.limits: Three authored puzzles, fixed mirror positions, no procedural levels, persistent saves, audio, multiplayer, or physical optics simulation. Refresh loses progress. Solutions are encoded locally and hints can reveal them. This pack is a consolidated implementation specification and verification instruction, not a verbatim development transcript or one-shot claim. Reproduction should compare features and rules, not identical pixels. Record manual edits and actual browser coverage separately. Build record (2026-09-06): GPT-6 Astra with High reasoning in Codex; implemented then repaired equal-row beam alignment, SVG stacking, narrow enlarged controls and board-symbol sizing using Step 2. Original build passed 11 grouped Chromium checks; an independent agent rebuilt from the pack and passed 18 grouped checks plus exhaustive authored geometry. Cross-browser, physical-device and manual assistive-technology testing were not performed. The gallery preview and downloadable pack refer to Light Relay v1.

proof.startingPoint: A new standalone HTML file, inline CSS and JavaScript, no dependencies or external services.
proof.interventions: Authored from the consolidated build specification. Browser and visual checks required equal CSS grid rows for correct beam alignment, beam SVG above mirror backgrounds with pointer-events:none, wrapping and shrinking enlarged controls, and fixed-size board symbols to avoid overlap at 200% root text. Those repairs are included in Step 2. No external assets or manual user setup were required. This is an ordered build/verification pack, not a one-shot or verbatim transcript claim.
proof.checks: 11 grouped Chromium checks passed on 2026-09-06: exact CSP and opaque-origin readiness; storage denial; unsolved/locked state; hint coordinates without movement and hint-preserving undo; first-chamber best/hint tie; chamber solutions at 2/3/6 rotations; final completion; full reset and keyboard actions/focus; widths 320/375/768/1024/1440/1600 and 200% root text; equal cell geometry; emulated touch; no script errors or external requests. Real desktop, solved and mobile screenshots captured. Enlarged source/receiver symbols and text overflow checked separately.
proof.reproductionNotes: A separate fresh-context GPT-6 Astra (High) agent rebuilt from this prompt pack in a clean directory without inspecting the original source or images. 18 Chromium check groups passed. An independent exhaustive geometry check covered all 4/16/64 orientations and confirmed unique solutions with minima 2/3/6. Reproduction needed an SVG stacking repair, included in Step 2; final Step 2 was reapplied and checks rerun. This establishes matching features, not identical pixels or one-shot success. Chromium only; no physical-device or screen-reader study.

recipe.title: Glyph Loom
recipe.summary: Draw one tile. Watch it become a repeating pattern.

steps.title: Build Glyph Loom
steps.text:
Build a complete standalone glyph-loom.html with inline CSS and JavaScript. It is a 16-by-16 binary pixel-pattern editor with mirrored drawing, a live 3-by-3 repeat preview and selectable ASCII output. No packages, external assets, network, storage, accounts, audio, eval or form submission. Include a viewport meta and CSP meta exactly: default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; connect-src 'none'. It must work in iframe sandbox='allow-scripts' with opaque origin. After synchronous initialization send window.parent.postMessage({type:'pls-demo-ready'}, '*').

Design an original near-black printmaking instrument: canvas #080808, panels #111111, gray hairline borders #383838, text #f2f2f2 and secondary #b8b8b8. Large condensed system sans uppercase GLYPH LOOM heading; system monospace for labels and controls. Subtitle: Draw one tile. Watch it become a pattern. Header includes 16 x 16 / PATTERN WORKSHOP. Desktop uses two equal-width panels, editor left and repeated cloth preview right, with a restrained ASCII +---+ divider motif, generous padding, rounded 12px panel corners and a bottom output section. Below 700px stack editor, repeat preview and output. Colored pixels are the only accent; controls remain grayscale. Use Mint #a8ebcb initially, Amber #edc583 and Violet #c7b6ef palette options. Active ink uses the selected color; empty pixels use #111111. Color changes affect only preview, never binary data or ASCII. Use clear selected states, 44px minimum ordinary controls, 16px body type, focus outline, normal wrapping, no forced motion and no horizontal page overflow at 320px or 200% root text.

Store a row-major array of exactly 256 zeros/ones in session memory. Initial Diamond preset uses zero-based x,y: 5 <= abs(x-7.5)+abs(y-7.5) <= 7. Steps preset: (floor(x/2)+floor(y/2))%4===0. Orbit preset: 25 <= (x-7.5)^2+(y-7.5)^2 <= 42. Each preset replaces the tile as one undoable action, leaving tool/mirror/palette unchanged. Presets are deterministic.

Editor: square canvas with internal resolution 512x512 and 16x16 cells, thin grid lines, and a visible cursor outline with non-color corner marks. Keep CSS aspect ratio 1. Make canvas focusable with role=application and an accessible name explaining keyboard use; keep instructions visible outside. Show current one-based row/column and count of inked cells. Start cursor at row 1 column 1. Ink brush sets cells to 1; Erase sets to 0, never toggle. Mirror mode initially Both axes; other modes None and Left/right. Left/right stamps (x,y) and (15-x,y). Both axes also stamps (x,15-y) and (15-x,15-y); deduplicate positions. Changing mirror mode affects future marks only.

Mouse/pen/touch drawing: pointerdown on editor starts one stroke and focuses editor; map client coordinates via its bounding box, clamp 0..15, capture pointer. Accept only primary pointer and primary button. On pointermove during the same captured pointer, interpolate skipped cells with integer Bresenham line, applying current ink/erase and mirror mode. On pointerup, pointercancel or lostpointercapture finish the stroke as ONE undoable action if tile changed; handle termination idempotently. Hover may update cursor but does not draw. Keep touch-action:none scoped to the drawing canvas; page elsewhere scrolls. Never lose completed marks on pointer exit. Show live preview/count/output during drawing. Before any other state-changing control action finalize any active stroke.

Keyboard when editor focused: Arrow keys move cursor one cell and clamp at edges, Home moves column to 1, End to 16; prevent default only handled keys. Space or Enter stamps at cursor as one undoable action, retains canvas focus. Provide equivalent labeled Row and Column number inputs (1..16, initially 1), and a Stamp cell button using the same tool and mirror rules; reject empty/noninteger/out-of-range values with a visible status, no drawing or history change. Arrow movement and pointer movement keep those coordinate inputs synchronized. No global shortcut handler that intercepts text editing.

Undo and Redo restore whole tile snapshots; maximum 50 previous actions, clear redo after a new changed action. Disable unavailable controls. No-op stamps/presets/clear produce no history entry. Clear tile zeros all cells; Invert tile swaps 0/1; each is undoable. Reset workshop restores original Diamond, Ink, Both axes, Mint, cursor 1/1, empty history and redo. Settings/cursor changes alone are not undo entries. Undo/redo restore tile only, preserving settings. Show polite live status with action outcome (not every pointermove).

Repeat preview is another square canvas of internal size 768x768, drawing the same tile repeated 3 times horizontally and vertically (48x48 cells). No editing or grid lines in repeat preview; give it an image role and meaningful accessible name. Label it 3 x 3 REPEAT with dynamic ink count and coverage percent rounded to nearest whole percent. Update both canvases on tile or palette change. Use crisp integer canvas rects.

Output: labeled read-only textarea containing exactly 16 lines of 16 characters each, # for ink and . for empty, no trailing newline. Update after every tile change. Add Select ASCII to focus/select the complete output for manual copying, plus Copy ASCII that attempts navigator.clipboard.writeText and then document.execCommand('copy') if necessary. Confirm Copied only on success; otherwise say Copy unavailable. Use Select ASCII and your browser copy command. Guard missing APIs; clipboard denial must never break drawing. No file-download action inside this sandbox. The host distributes the recipe separately. Display: Session only. Reload clears edits. ASCII is a tile, not an image file. This is a drawing tool, not AI generation. Use inert textContent/value for text. All displayed metrics must derive from tile state.

steps.title: Verify and repair
steps.text: Run the finished HTML in a browser inside an iframe with sandbox='allow-scripts'. Verify readiness message comes from opaque origin null, no external requests and no script errors. Check all three presets against their supplied formulas, 256-cell state, 16x16 #/. output, and matching preview. Clear; stamp row 2 column 3 with Both axes -> exactly (2,3),(2,14),(15,3),(15,14) in one-based coordinates; repeat stamp is a no-op; Undo clears all four; Redo restores. Change mode to None, erase one cell -> count 3; undo restores 4. Clear again; pointer drag must fill skipped cells with Bresenham and undo as one action; exercise touch and pointer termination. Verify Left/right, keyboard edge clamping and Space/Enter, coordinate validation (empty, 0, 17, fractional), no-op history, redo invalidation and 50-entry history cap. Invert twice restores exact output. Palette change leaves ASCII unchanged. Reset restores every initial setting and clears history. Test copy success and denial separately; Select ASCII must select full output. Inspect widths 320,375,768,1024,1440,1600 and 200% root text; repair overflow, clipped controls, canvas distortion or unreadable text. Check dynamic metrics and repeat rendering. Capture real screenshots of the running editor and a changed pattern. Rebuild separately from this pack in an empty directory and run the same behavioral checks. Record actual model, interventions, test coverage and reproduction result; do not claim unrun browser or independent-user coverage. Preserve the no-network, opaque-origin, session-memory design.

recipe.setup: Open an empty folder in Codex, paste Step 1, then Step 2 in the same task. Open glyph-loom.html in a modern browser or serve it with a static server. No packages, credentials, paid services or assets are needed. The PLS PROMPT gallery supplies separate host chrome and recipe download.
recipe.customize: Change the three preset formulas or ink palettes. Keep formulas deterministic and colors readable. To change tile dimensions, update both canvases, coordinate validation, mirror math, repeat geometry and ASCII dimensions together. Add persistence only as a separately designed standalone feature; the gallery demo uses session memory.
recipe.limits: Binary 16x16 tiles; three ink palettes; ASCII text output only. No image import/export, layers, persistent saves, collaborative editing or AI generation. Clipboard access can be denied by the sandbox; Select ASCII provides manual copying. Pixel-level pointer targets are small on narrow screens; keyboard and explicit row/column stamping provide precise alternatives. This is a consolidated build-and-verification pack, not a verbatim development transcript or a one-shot guarantee. Build record (2026-09-07): Codex / GPT-6 Astra High; original passed 13 browser check groups after an enlarged-settings layout repair; independent fresh-context agent reproduction passed 19 groups. Reproduction matches behavior, not identical pixels. Chromium only; copy branches injected and touch emulated; no physical-device or screen-reader study. The demo and this download match Glyph Loom v1.

proof.interventions: Authored from the consolidated specification. Browser test harness required scrolling the editor into view before a real pointer-cancel check. No manual user setup or external assets. Real screenshots captured; visual review repaired enlarged settings labels.
proof.reproductionNotes: A separate fresh-context GPT-6 Astra High agent rebuilt from these two prompts alone in a new empty directory, without inspecting original source or images. 19 actual Chromium check groups passed, including all preset formulas, repeat pixels, history cap, diagonal/horizontal drawing, pointer termination, touch emulation, invalid inputs, clipboard branches, six widths at normal and 200% root text. No recipe or HTML repairs needed; a harness-only scroll-into-view fix preceded final checks. This validates matching behavior, not identical pixels or independent-human usability. recipe.title: Curve Cabinet
recipe.summary: Shape a motion curve. Compare the feel. Keep the CSS.

steps.title: Build Curve Cabinet
steps.text:
Create curve-cabinet.html: a complete standalone cubic-Bezier CSS easing workshop with inline HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No libraries, external assets, storage, network, accounts, audio, eval or forms. Include viewport meta and CSP meta: default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; connect-src 'none'. It must work in an opaque-origin iframe sandbox='allow-scripts'. After initialization send window.parent.postMessage({type:'pls-demo-ready'}, '*').

Visual thesis: a compact near-black motion instrument, with a large square Cartesian curve graph left and a right-side motion comparison bench. Canvas #080808; surfaces #111111; hairlines #383838; controls #777777 borders; text #f2f2f2 and secondary #b8b8b8. Condensed system sans uppercase CURVE CABINET title and system monospace interface. Subtitle: Shape a motion curve. Compare the feel. Keep the CSS. Functional graph/markers use mint #a8ebcb and amber #edc583; controls stay grayscale. Use restrained ASCII +---+ dividers, fine gridlines, rounded 12px graph/bench surfaces and ample padding. Desktop two columns, below 760px stack graph, settings and comparison; useful controls and results immediately visible. Body 16px, controls at least 14px in rem, ordinary buttons and draggable handles at least 44x44px. Text-relative auto-fit fields must reflow at 320px and 200% root text without clipping. No decorative animation.

Core math: endpoints P0=(0,0), P3=(1,1), editable P1=(x1,y1), P2=(x2,y2), all coordinates constrained to [0,1]. Cubic coordinate B(t,a,b)=3*(1-t)^2*t*a + 3*(1-t)*t^2*b + t^3. Given elapsed fraction u, solve B(t,x1,x2)=u with 40 iterations of bisection and return B(t,y1,y2). Return exact 0/1 at endpoints. Do NOT substitute t=u; x1>x2 remains valid. Round user-edited coordinates to 2 decimals. Duration integer 200..3000 milliseconds in increments of 100.

Initial preset Ease=(0.25,0.10,0.25,1), duration=1200, elapsed=0.5, paused. Other exact presets: Linear=(0,0,1,1), Glide=(0.16,1,0.30,1), S-curve=(0.65,0,0.35,1). Preset buttons show aria-pressed based on matching committed coordinates; otherwise show Custom. Applying any curve or duration change pauses animation and preserves current elapsed fraction.

Graph maps elapsed x left-to-right, eased progress y bottom-to-top. Use SVG for grid, diagonal linear reference, cubic path, two tangent lines and current sample dot. SVG is a data visualization, not artwork. Put graph inside a padded square surface so endpoint handles fit inside the page. Overlay two real numbered button handles at corresponding P1/P2 positions; accessible names identify control point and coordinates. Button handles support primary mouse/pen/touch drag with pointer capture, same-pointer moves only, coordinate mapping through plot bounding rect, clamp and round; ignore secondary buttons/pointers. Retain capture until pointerup/cancel/lost capture. Dragging updates curve, fields, output, sample and comparison immediately, pauses animation and preserves elapsed. Scope touch-action:none to handles; page elsewhere scrolls. Handles accept ArrowLeft/Right to move x by .01, ArrowUp/Down y by .01; Shift uses .1; clamp/round; prevent default only handled arrows; retain focus. No global keyboard traps. Show instructions and axis meanings.

Provide labeled number inputs X1,Y1,X2,Y2 and Duration (ms), plus Apply values. Applying uses all five fields atomically: reject blank, nonfinite, out-of-range values; duration must be an integer multiple of 100. Invalid apply pauses but leaves committed curve, duration, sample, preset and export unchanged, preserves entered text, sets aria-invalid on bad fields and announces a readable correction. Valid apply rounds coordinates to two decimals, normalizes fields, clears invalid states and updates everything. Editing fields alone must not affect committed state or animation. Handle/preset/reset actions replace pending field text with current valid state.

Comparison bench: two horizontal lanes labeled Your curve and Linear, each with a square marker whose left percentage is based on a full-width position wrapper ending one marker-width before track edge so endpoints stay inside. Your curve marker uses eased progress, Linear uses elapsed. Both share the same duration/time. Text outputs expose elapsed percent, eased percent and signed percentage-point lead (eased minus elapsed), rounded to one decimal. Graph sample dot is (elapsed,eased). Add a labeled Timeline range input min=0,max=1000,step=1, initially 500; input scrubs elapsed and pauses.

Play resumes from current fraction or restarts at 0 if complete; Pause freezes fraction; Replay starts at 0 and plays; Reset cabinet restores Ease/1200/50%/paused, clears input errors and pending drag, updates all fields/output. Use requestAnimationFrame and timestamp-based elapsed so speed does not depend on frame rate; exactly stop at 100%, no loop, no autoplay. Maintain at most one RAF; cancel it on pause, reset, curve changes, scrubbing and document hidden. Returning visible must stay paused. Reflect state in visible Paused/Playing/Complete text and Play/Pause label. Respect prefers-reduced-motion initially and dynamically: pause when enabled, disable Play and Replay, show Reduced motion: use the timeline. Scrubbing, curve editing and reset remain available. Turning preference off does not autoplay. Status is aria-live polite for actions/errors, not animation frame updates.

Output is a labeled read-only textarea containing exactly two CSS declarations on separate lines: transition-duration: 1200ms; and transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1); for initial state. Values always reflect committed curve and duration; canonical numbers have no unnecessary trailing zeros. Add Select CSS (focus and select whole output) and Copy CSS: guarded navigator.clipboard.writeText then guarded document.execCommand('copy') fallback; confirm only actual success, otherwise say Copy unavailable. Use Select CSS and your browser copy command. No download inside sandbox; host supplies recipe separately. Display limitation: Session only. Coordinates stay between 0 and 1; no overshoot or spring physics. CSS sets timing, not what property moves. Use inert textContent/value for dynamic text.

steps.title: Verify and repair
steps.text: Run the finished HTML in Chromium inside an iframe sandbox='allow-scripts'. Confirm opaque-origin readiness, no network requests and no script errors. Independently calculate Bezier progress using bisection; initial Ease at 50% is about 80.2403%, not the cubic at t=.5. Verify all four exact presets at elapsed 0, .25, .5, .75, 1 and custom crossing x1=.9,x2=.1. Confirm lane positions, sample dot, percentage-point lead, current-preset state and canonical CSS match committed math. Test valid coordinate/duration apply and invalid blank, NaN-like input, -0.1,1.1,duration 250/199/3100; invalid apply keeps prior curve/duration/export and entered values. Verify graph drag clamp and rounding, mouse and touch emulation, pointer termination, secondary-pointer rejection, arrow increments .01/Shift .1, edge clamps and focus. Verify Play/Pause/resume/Replay/completion, changing curve during play, timeline scrub stopping play, complete reset, hidden-document pause and no auto-resume. Test reduced-motion enabled at start and dynamically; no animation and scrubbing works. Check copy success/denial with explicit injected API branches and Select CSS selection; do not claim real permissions from injected tests. Inspect 320,375,768,1024,1440,1600 widths and 200% root text; repair overflow/clipped fields/handle edges. Capture real initial and changed-curve screenshots. Separately rebuild from this pack in an empty directory without original code or screenshots and verify those behaviors; record actual model, repairs and coverage honestly. Keep this as a consolidated build-and-verification pack rather than a one-shot guarantee.

recipe.title: Chance Drawer
recipe.summary: Predict a token draw. Compare exact odds with thousands of samples.

steps.title: Build Chance Drawer
steps.text:
Create chance-drawer.html, a standalone probability workshop with inline HTML/CSS/JavaScript and no packages, assets, accounts, payments, storage, network, eval, audio or form submission. Include viewport meta and CSP meta: default-src 'none'; script-src 'unsafe-inline'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; connect-src 'none'. It must work in an opaque-origin iframe sandbox='allow-scripts'. After initialization send window.parent.postMessage({type:'pls-demo-ready'}, '*').

Visual thesis: a near-black analytical instrument with a wide token drawer on the left and a probability readout on the right; an outcome-distribution strip below. Canvas #080808, surfaces #111111, borders #383838, controls #777777, text #f2f2f2 and #b8b8b8. Large condensed system sans CHANCE DRAWER title, monospace controls, restrained +---+ ASCII separator. Color only in data marks: Mint A tokens #a8ebcb, Amber B tokens #edc583; each token has a visible letter, not color alone. Native controls stay grayscale. Header subtitle: Predict a draw. Test the odds. Desktop two-column working surface; stack below 760px. Body 1rem, labels at least .875rem, actions min-height 44px, strong focus, natural wrapping, no horizontal overflow at widths 320/375/768/1024/1440/1600 and 200% root text at 320. No animation, autoplay or timer.

Committed experiment starts A count=4, B count=6, draw size=3, replacement off, event Exactly 2 A. A and B integer counts each 0..20, total must be 1..40; draw size integer 1..10 and at most total without replacement. Event choices Exactly, At least, At most, with integer target 0..draw size. Labeled number inputs for A tokens, B tokens, Draw size, Target A; checkbox Replace after each pick; select Event; Apply experiment button. Editing fields changes nothing until Apply. Atomically reject blank/nonfinite/fractional/out-of-range/inconsistent values; preserve entered text, committed display/distribution/trials and mark invalid fields aria-invalid; give readable polite error. Valid Apply commits all fields, normalizes fields, clears trial results/history and errors, renders fresh bag and distribution. Do not silently clamp. Presets: Balanced = 4/6/3/no replacement/Exactly 2; Rare A = 1/9/3/no replacement/At least 1; Replacement = 4/6/3/replacement/Exactly 2. Selecting preset immediately replaces pending text, applies experiment and clears trials. Reset workshop restores Balanced and no trials/errors.

Exact probability: build distribution P(K=k), k=0..draw size, by dynamic programming over pick count and A count. Start dp[0]=1. With replacement pA=A/(A+B) at each pick; without replacement pA=(A-k)/(A+B-picksAlreadyMade) for reachable states, pB=(B-(picksAlreadyMade-k))/(A+B-picksAlreadyMade). Add each branch into next dp. Skip zero-mass states; no factorials, Monte Carlo approximations for exact probability, or impossible negative paths. Event sums distribution for k===target, k>=target or k<=target. Show exact event percent to two decimals (initial 30.00%), expected A per draw = n*A/(A+B) to two decimals (initial 1.20), replacement mode and a visible event sentence. All metrics derive from committed data. Show all distribution outcomes as a horizontal/vertical bar chart with k labels, exact percent text and explicit Selected event text on qualifying outcomes, including zero-probability outcomes; no color-only selection. Visual chart optional aria-hidden if equivalent semantic probability list is present. Explain briefly: exact odds model every possible draw; sampled results vary.

Bag visualization shows all committed A/B tokens, labeled and grouped with count legend. Draw once samples a whole draw of n picks: use Math.random at each pick, compare to remaining A/remaining total; decrement selected type only without replacement. Each new trial starts with a fresh full bag, so trials are independent. Track trials and matches; Draw 100 runs exactly 100 more synchronous bounded trials. Disable both draw buttons before a request would exceed total cap 10,000; show cap clearly. Show sampled match rate to two decimals or em dash when zero; signed sampled-minus-exact percentage-point difference to two decimals or dash when zero; normalize rounded negative zero. Show current trial's ordered A/B pick tokens and its A count plus Matches event/Outside event text. Show last eight trials newest first, each trial number, ordered token letters and outcome. Batch simulation retains the final eight actual trials and last draw, not eight invented summaries. No auto simulation, statistical guarantees, forecasting, crypto randomness or gambling framing. Clear trials resets trials/matches/history/last draw, preserving committed experiment AND any unsubmitted text. Clearing enables capped buttons. Valid apply/preset/reset also clears trials. Actions retain keyboard focus (Select report intentionally focuses its textarea; Copy fallback restores focus to Copy). When sampling disables the focused draw button at the cap, move focus to Clear trials; native buttons and inputs work with Enter/Space as applicable. Announce action summaries politely, not every individual trial inside a batch.

Include a labeled read-only Experiment report textarea with committed A/B/n/replacement/event, exact percent and expected A, trials, matches and observed percent. Update only on committed or trial changes. Select report focuses/selects the whole textarea. Copy report first tries guarded navigator.clipboard.writeText then guarded document.execCommand('copy'); show Copied only after actual success, otherwise say Copy unavailable. Use Select report and your browser copy command. No downloads inside the sandbox. Use textContent/value for dynamic content. Visible limits: Session only. Pseudorandom samples; not a forecasting tool. At most 40 tokens, 10 picks and 10,000 trials. The gallery supplies a separate recipe download.

steps.title: Verify and repair
steps.text: Verify and repair the standalone file inside iframe sandbox='allow-scripts' with the exact CSP. Test initial full distribution [20,60,20,0] only for a DIFFERENT experiment A=2,B=4,n=3 without replacement; for actual Balanced A=4,B=6,n=3 the distribution must be [16.6666667,50,30,3.3333333] percent, sum 100, exact 2 event 30%, expected 1.2. Rare A at least 1 =30%; Replacement exact 2 =28.8%. Check all three event operators against hand-calculated probabilities, target 0/n, zero A, zero B, drawing whole bag, and n=10 with replacement from a single token. Cross-check DP independently with combination/binomial formulas over every allowed count and draw size. Reject blanks, fractions, both counts zero, target beyond n, oversize draw without replacement and counts outside limits without changing committed state, trials or report. Editing alone must not change state. Presets and reset discard pending edits; Clear trials preserves them. Inject deterministic Math.random values in test context to exercise all-A/all-B and depletion paths; ordinary runs remain random. Check Draw once, exactly 100 added trials, newest-eight history, cap at 10,000 and re-enabling after clear. Verify sampled rate and signed percentage-point gap, including rounded zero. Test full selection and injected copy success/denial. Confirm readiness origin null, denied storage, no external requests or script errors; keyboard controls/focus (including capped draw moving focus to Clear trials and Copy fallback restoring Copy focus), six widths, 200% root text and touch emulation. Capture actual initial and sampled screenshots. Repair problems, rerun affected checks and report exact coverage and interventions. Rebuild independently from this pack in an empty directory, without original code or screenshots, and rerun behavior tests. Do not claim identical pixels, one-shot success, cross-browser, physical-device or independent-human testing unless performed.

recipe.setup: Open an empty directory in Codex. Paste Step 1, then Step 2 in the same task. Open chance-drawer.html in a modern browser or serve it with a static server. No packages, accounts, keys, images or paid services are required. PLS PROMPT supplies separate gallery framing and recipe download.
recipe.customize: Change token colors and preset experiments while retaining visible A/B labels and valid count limits. Add an event by updating its acceptance predicate, labels and independent probability checks. Larger bags, draw counts or batch sizes require revisiting numeric precision, rendering cost and caps together.
recipe.limits: Session memory only; two token types, at most 40 tokens, 10 picks and 10,000 trials. Exact probabilities assume uniformly sampled tokens; trials use Math.random and can differ from theoretical odds. No persistence, import, forecasting, cryptographic randomness or external data. Clipboard may be denied; Select report supports manual copying. Consolidated build/verification pack, not a verbatim transcript or one-shot guarantee. Reproduction compares behavior, not identical pixels. Build record (2026-09-09): GPT-6 Astra High; original 13 Chromium groups, independent reproduction 14 groups; both checked 8,590 configurations against independent formulas. Chromium only; touch emulated, clipboard branches injected; no physical-device, Safari, screen-reader or independent-human study. Demo and recipe match Chance Drawer v1.

proof.startingPoint: New standalone HTML file with inline CSS/JavaScript. No dependencies, assets, credentials or services.
proof.interventions: Authored from a consolidated build specification. Review identified focus loss when sampling disabled its focused button and when Copy used a textarea fallback; repaired cap focus transfer to Clear trials and Copy focus restoration. Explicit grayscale native input accent added. These requirements are included in the final pack. Original preview captures use actual working states. No manual user setup or external assets.

Rebuild repaired an invalid CSS grid parenthesis, set grayscale checkbox accent and applied clarified cap-focus handling. Same final spec; no original code supplied. Behavior reproduced, not identical pixels. Chromium only; touch and clipboard branches emulated/injected; no physical-device, screen-reader or independent-human study.
